subject.title: trusted-proxy auth: support fallback/default user when identity header is absent

question: Should trusted-proxy auth support an explicit fallback identity when the configured identity header is absent on a request from a trusted proxy source?
rationale: The implementation path is mechanically clear, but it changes the auth boundary from per-request identity evidence to proxy-source plus configured principal, which automation should not decide.

options.title: Approve narrow fallback mode
options.body: Add an explicit single-principal fallback config with fail-closed defaults, audit/docs/schema updates, and tests for proxy source, loopback, required headers, and allowlist semantics.

options.title: Keep fail-closed identity headers
options.body: Reject headerless trusted-proxy identity and document Cloudflare Zero Trust IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket setups as unsupported for this auth mode.

options.title: Require live Cloudflare proof first
options.body: Ask for reproducible Cloudflare Tunnel proof before deciding whether OpenClaw should add a fallback identity surface.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow fallback mode
recommendation.body: Add an explicit single-principal fallback config with fail-closed defaults, audit/docs/schema updates, and tests for proxy source, loopback, required headers, and allowlist semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is assigned, already separated this report from the local-direct fallback cluster, and has recent commits on the adjacent trusted-proxy auth boundary.
